text:
harper.sales: ACME POC just hit a weird combo: function_call + json mode -> schema ValidationError + occasional truncated streams. They asked if this is on their side or ours.

mina.eng: Can you share a failing assistant payload and the request shape (sanitized)? Also which model variant?

harper.sales: They use `gptx-4o-hosted`. Request (sanitized): ```json {"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"batch ingest"}],"functions":[{"name":"record_event","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"},"meta":{"type":"object"}},"required":["id"],"additionalProperties":false}}],"function_call":"auto","mode":"json"} ```

jules.sre: On our side I see per-route bursts and a small window of 429s plus some upstream stream resets around 13:17. Logs: "[13:17:22] route tooling-v2: x-rl-remaining=0 -> 429; [13:17:23] stream closed by upstream (ECONNRESET)". That matches truncated responses.

mina.eng: For schema failures we need the raw assistant function_call. harper can you paste one failed assistant response?

harper.sales: ACME pasted this snippet: `{"name":"record_event","arguments":"{\"id\":\"evt-9\",\"meta\":\"tags:\"alpha\"}"}` — arguments ended up as a double-escaped string. They also showed another: `{"name":"record_event","arguments":null}`.

mina.eng: Double-escaped string -> client or SDK serialized twice; null -> model primitive where object expected. Two quick remediations: client-side sanitize (JSON.parse + type-check) or server-side lenient pre-parser that will attempt to un-stringify and coerce primitives into an object for known functions.

noah.se: ACME also asked: if we raise their qps for the POC, is there a cost bump? They worry about being charged unexpectedly.

jules.sre: Short-term ops: I can raise their per-route burst and org bucket for 90 minutes to reduce 429s while they run heavy batches. We can mark it as a courtesy POC increase; billing will not be changed automatically — sales will confirm any extended increases.

harper.sales: I'll handle the billing note. For now they asked for a quick workaround they can apply today.

mina.eng: Quick client snippet to unblock (send to ACME):
```js
// decode arguments if string
if (typeof resp.arguments === 'string') {
  try { resp.arguments = JSON.parse(resp.arguments) } catch (e) { /* log + return validation error */ }
}
// coerce primitives for known fn
if (resp.arguments == null || typeof resp.arguments !== 'object') {
  resp.arguments = { id: String(resp.arguments) }
}
```

harper.sales: ACME can patch that now. Anything we can do server-side to reduce noise for them?

mina.eng: We can deploy a canary pre-parser behind a tenant flag `poc.parse_fallback` that: 1) tries to parse stringified arguments, 2) wraps primitives for specific function signatures, and 3) strips helper keys starting with `__` before schema validation. It will emit metrics `poc_parses`, `poc_wrapped`, `poc_stripped`.

jules.sre: I'll also apply a temporary increase: org acme_poc qps from 180 -> 420 and route tooling-v2 burst to 320 for 90m. I'll add alerting if `ingress.stream_aborts` spikes.

noah.se: ACME asked a security question: does the canary pre-parser log full argument content? They have data residency concerns and want to ensure PII isn't sent to logs.

mina.eng: Good catch. The canary will only log structured metadata and emit counts; it will redact values and never persist full arguments. We'll note that in the tenant flag doc and only enable for the tenant after consent.

harper.sales: Customer wants the lenient mode opt-in plus the temporary qps bump. They also want a written summary for their security team.

mina.eng: I'll prepare a short summary: what the pre-parser does, metrics collected (counts only), retention policy (7 days for POC logs), and that no full payloads are persisted.

jules.sre: Done wedge: I've bumped their qps and enabled extra logging to monitor aborts. Deploy-bot starting canary: `parse-fallback` -> canary at 2026-03-21T19:05:00Z.

deploy-bot: Deployment started for branch `poc/parse-fallback` -> canary.

harper.sales: ACME validated after applying client patch and with our canary + qps bump — truncation stopped and validation errors dropped by ~99%. They reported one remaining case where model returned `{"id":"x","__meta_hint":"v"}` which was stripped by the pre-parser.

mina.eng: Next steps: 1) we'll keep the tenant flag on for the remainder of the POC, 2) sales to confirm billing stance for extended qps, 3) engineering will prepare a short doc for ACME security covering logging/redaction.

harper.sales: I'll send the summary and request SOC2 redaction note. Thanks for the quick help :pray:
